story.title:

story.image_alt: Rudralife Siddha Mala displayed with its presentation box
story.caption: SINCE 2001 · A RUDRALIFE SIGNATURE CREATION
paragraphs: Rudralife was founded in 2001 by Dr. Tanay Seetha with a single purpose: to make authentic Rudraksha, and honest guidance about it, available to every seeker.
Twenty-five years on, the Siddha Mala remains one of its signature creations—a registered Rudralife combination that brings 1 to 14 Mukhi, Gauri Shankar and Ganesh Rudraksha together in one mala.
Every recommendation still begins the same way it did in 2001: by listening to the person who will wear the mala.

beads.text: Explore each sacred form, its traditional meaning and its place in the complete combination.
beads.note: Traditional associations are based on spiritual beliefs. Individual experiences vary.

items.name: 1 Mukhi
items.desc: The half-moon Rudraksha is traditionally associated with Lord Shiva, inner awareness and a deeper spiritual connection.

items.name: 2 Mukhi
items.desc: Representing the union of Shiva and Shakti, the two-faced bead is traditionally worn for harmony and togetherness.

items.name: 3 Mukhi
items.desc: Associated with Agni, the three-faced Rudraksha symbolises transformation, confidence and freedom from the past.

items.name: 4 Mukhi
items.desc: The four-faced Rudraksha is associated with Brahma and traditionally chosen for learning, creativity and expression.

items.name: 5 Mukhi
items.desc: Associated with Kalagni Rudra, this bead has a special place in meditation and everyday spiritual practice.

items.name: 6 Mukhi
items.desc: The six-faced Rudraksha represents Kartikeya and is traditionally associated with focus, willpower and discipline.

items.name: 7 Mukhi
items.desc: Representing Mahalakshmi, the seven-faced bead is traditionally worn with aspirations for prosperity and abundance.

items.name: 8 Mukhi
items.desc: Associated with Ganesha, this Rudraksha symbolises wisdom and overcoming obstacles on your chosen path.

items.name: 9 Mukhi
items.desc: The nine-faced Rudraksha represents Durga and is traditionally associated with courage, strength and protection.

items.name: 10 Mukhi
items.desc: Associated with Vishnu, the ten-faced bead is traditionally worn for protection and a sense of inner steadiness.

items.name: 11 Mukhi
items.desc: The eleven-faced Rudraksha represents Hanuman and symbolises strength, devotion and fearlessness.

items.name: 12 Mukhi
items.desc: Representing the Sun, the twelve-faced Rudraksha is traditionally associated with radiance, leadership and confidence.

items.name: 13 Mukhi
items.desc: The thirteen-faced Rudraksha is associated with Indra and Kamadeva, and traditionally chosen for fulfilment and attraction.

items.name: 14 Mukhi
items.desc: Known as Deva Mani, the fourteen-faced Rudraksha is traditionally associated with intuition, clear judgement and protection.

items.name: Gauri Shankar
items.desc: Two naturally joined Rudraksha beads symbolise the union of Shiva and Parvati, and harmony in family and relationships.

items.name: Ganesh
items.desc: Distinguished by a natural trunk-like projection, Ganesh Rudraksha symbolises wisdom and the blessing of new beginnings.

beads.breakdown: 3 each of 2–7 Mukhi (18) + 1 each of 8–14 Mukhi (7) + Half-Moon 1 Mukhi, Gauri Shankar and Ganesh (3) = 28 beads.

education.title:
Understanding
your Siddha Mala.
education.text: A little understanding makes the connection more meaningful.

items.a: The Siddha Mala brings together 1 to 14 Mukhi, Gauri Shankar and Ganesh Rudraksha. The listed composition contains 28 beads across 16 distinct forms. Repeated Mukhi forms are part of that composition, not separate varieties.

items.q: How many beads does the mala contain?
items.a: The source-confirmed configuration contains three each of 2 to 7 Mukhi, one each of 8 to 14 Mukhi, one Half-Moon 1 Mukhi, one Gauri Shankar and one Ganesh: 28 in total. Ask your consultant to confirm the exact configuration of the variant you choose.

items.q: How should I choose my mala?
items.a: Your intentions, preferences and the available bead grades and finishes can guide your choice. A Rudralife expert can explain these differences and recommend an appropriate combination without a consultation charge.

spiritual.image_alt: Lord Shiva and Rudraksha, from Rudralife’s Mahashivratri article
spiritual.caption: A SACRED STORY, PASSED THROUGH GENERATIONS
paragraphs: In the tradition retold by Rudralife, Shiva meditates for the well-being of humanity. His tears of compassion fall to the earth and become the first Rudraksha trees—a sacred story that gives these beads their enduring association with devotion.

The name brings together Rudra, a name of Shiva, and Aksha, associated with his eyes or tears. For a wearer, the mala can be a quiet reminder of compassion, reflection and a regular spiritual practice.
Siddha Mala gathers different Rudraksha forms into one personal companion. The story is a matter of religious tradition, not a scientific account or a promise of particular results.

founder.name: Dr. Tanay Seetha
founder.title:
A life dedicated
to Rudraksha.
paragraphs: Dr. Tanay Seetha founded Rudralife in 2001 and has spent more than 25 years in Rudraksha research and spiritual guidance. His work began with a simple conviction: every seeker deserves authentic Rudraksha and honest advice about it.

Under his guidance, Rudralife created the Siddha Mala as a complete combination of 1 to 14 Mukhi, Gauri Shankar and Ganesh Rudraksha. He has shared his knowledge on national platforms including Republic Bharat, and continues to lead the Rudralife expert panel.
